title: Professional Development
description: Provides an overview of the career paths available to Film and Media Studies students as well as a practical understanding of how various industries operate. Also matches students with careers that meet their intellectual and professional goals.

title: Lighting for the Moving Image
description: A workshop/seminar approach to explorations in how lighting affects the moving image, Students gain hands-on experience working with multiple lighting scenarios including fixtures, greenscreen and natural light.
prerequisites_raw: Film and Media Studies 46 or consent of instructor.

title: Sound Production
description: A workshop approach to explorations of sound recording, editing, and mixing. Students learn how to use professional sound editing software with an emphasis on editing for film including in 5.1-surround sound.
prerequisites_raw: Film Studies 104 or 105; consent of instructor.

title: Advanced Sound Production
description: This advanced course takes a workshop approach to explorations and methods of sound post-production, focusing on audio editing, audio repair, mixing and delivery. Lectures complement the hands-on labs by covering theoretical concepts, examination of significant films, and learning key techniques in sound production.
prerequisites_raw: Film and Media Studies 115, consent of instructor.

title: Editing
description: A workshop approach to explorations of editing, color correction and sound mixing in project production.
prerequisites_raw: Film Studies 104 and 105; consent of the instructor.

title: Sponsored Campus Production
description: An interface with campus "clients" who provide the budget and goals for crew projects.

title: Green Screen
description: A hands-on, project-based environmental media production course. Students work in teams to leverage their collective production skills and environmental knowledge to create short films, which premiere in the Pollock Theater at the end of the quarter.
